caption:
Some apps block paste on password fields with onPaste={(e) => e.preventDefault()}, usually "for security".

It doesn't add security. It punishes people who use long, random passwords from a password manager, so they switch to something short they can type.

NIST's digital identity guidelines say services should let users paste into password fields, for exactly this reason.

The same goes for "Confirm email" fields that block paste. Users retype, make a typo, and never get your emails.

Remove the handler and let the password manager do its job.

Source: NIST SP 800-63B, Digital Identity Guidelines (password verifiers).
